items: OpenAI has released a new image classifier that detects potential child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including AI-generated content.
The classifier reduces the number of flagged images by 48% while maintaining the same detection rate for abusive content, potentially easing the workload for content reviewers.

OpenAI is also implementing product warnings in ChatGPT to prevent users from seeking abusive material, with consequences for violations including temporary access suspension and potential account closure.

MANILA, Philippines – OpenAI announced the release of a new image classifier that can detect potential child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including AI-generated material.

The classifier can identify and help detect CSAM images, including those generated by AI. OpenAI said their new classifier “looks for visual signs of abuse, helping teams identify novel images that may not have been seen before.”

The classifier assigns scores to images it spots, helping content reviewers decide which images may require attention or intervention, and OpenAI said this will be made available to select companies through its API with no cost.
The company added that theirs is “the first CSAM classifier with broad availability that has a specific signal on indicating if CSAM may be AI generated.”

In early testing with partners, OpenAI said the new image classifier flags 48% fewer images but finds the same number of abusive images. This means a potential reduction of work for reviewers, as it noted that images flagged by the classifier are apparently twice as likely to contain abuse.
OpenAI also said it is implementing “product warnings in ChatGPT that interrupt attempts to find abusive material, explain the consequences, and point people toward help to stop harmful behavior.”

The company said their warning makes it clear that “sexualizing children causes harm, including when the requested material is AI-generated.” Aside from the warning, the flagged conversation will be removed, and access to ChatGPT will be paused for 24 hours, while specialist support will be available to help stop harmful behavior. Repeating the violation may, however, have consequences for a user account, such as longer restrictions, account closure, or reports to authorities.

OpenAI is also aiding developers by providing guidance, offering steps to prevent abuse, detect harmful content, as well as what-to-dos to help devs act if bad behaviors are starting to form. – Rappler.com
